The final metric of NQ is based on precision, recall and F1 among the examples where more than one annotators select NON-NULL answers and a model predicts a NON-NULL answer , to prevent a model always outputting unanswerable for achieving high scores. TyDi QA evaluation is based on recall, precision and byte-level F1 scores among the examples with answer annotations.
Human. We compare the models' performance with two types of human performance: binary and aggregate.

Human. The NQ authors provide upper-bound performance by estimating the performance of a single annotator (Single), and one of the aggregates of 25 annotators (Super). Super-annotator performance is considered as an NQ upper bound.
guideline: Compare model predictions to human annotator labels (binary agreement and majority agreement).

The evaluation script of NQ and TyDi QA calibrates the answer type for each question by thresholding long and short answers respectively to optimize the F1 score. We use the final predictions after this calibration process.
